answer: A memory-bound attestation protocol mitigates Sybil attacks by requiring agents to traverse dense pointer graphs held in fast SRAM. To register, each entity solves rapid access challenges inside an isolated challenge lagoon, exposing hollow nodes that lack dedicated memory. An attacker incurs scarce physical RAM capacity and bus bandwidth per concurrent identity, piercing any sable veil of virtualized proxies. However, high memory footprints unfairly penalize honest, lightweight edge agents.
